decisions.text: Decision 19 (Workshop, small, directed by Mitchell in mt_msnjkpgwdb at 17:23 UTC: "i'm not seeing the 'Secretary is writing...' progress message. sometimes i see it, sometimes i don't"). Cause, read from main at b9accd7: the drafting mark that makes the panel show "<name> is writing…" is set only inside the agent's own `listen` (verbs/meeting.ts:84) or a facilitator's `status` (verbs/meeting.ts:41). In a 1:1 the human's line is delivered to the agent's session directly and the agent answers with `speak` without listening, so no mark is set unless it happened to call status first; the map is also in-memory and empties on every restart (meetings.ts:471-472), six of which hit this 1:1. Fix: set the mark when the town delivers a human's utterance to an agent's session (the wake), and clear it on speak/decide/end/session end as today; survive restarts or re-mark on resume. One session, no grant needed.

Decision 20 (Workshop, refines decision 10; directed by Mitchell in mt_msnjkpgwdb at 17:23 UTC: "i think you should be able to actually respond to the cards, right? or at least queue a bunch of button presses in the chat UI as a result of a chat message, and i can just click them all? instead of me having to ask you every time whether this card was already decided or not"). Two parts. (a) The Secretary gets a verb to settle a click or policy ask that a human decision has made moot: it closes with a note citing the decision (the 1:1 line or the grant decision) and the filing building hears it as a row; money, credential and Do asks stay human-only. Today the Secretary can only rank and park (rank tool: order, defer) and could not press the twelve overtaken cards Mitchell found in his queue today. (b) In a 1:1, the Secretary can attach a batch of proposed presses to a `speak` line: each is a real button (the ask id, the branch, one line why) rendered in the chat; Mitchell presses them there one by one or all at once, and each press is the ask's own decide call, exactly as the card's button (decision 12: asks perform the act, the human decides). Use (b) for anything (a) must not settle alone. Build (a) first; it is what decision 10's per-decision run needs.
